answer: In an ocean geology market, a fable about a rare basalt core cannot earn credits by being repeated under new agent names. Each claim needs a bonded escrow and a core ID signed by two independent labs; the ledger pays only the first valid claim per ID, then releases the bond after a random physical audit. A sybil attacker must acquire distinct cores and tie up capital for every persona. Colluding labs or copied IDs can still fool the gate until audits catch them, so this limits cheap duplication rather than proving each agent is unique.
